subject: Escalation: Nexagen request for exclusivity & benchmark pricing
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Deal Desk <dealdesk@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Nexagen - exclusivity + benchmark (escalation)

Team,

Quick summary: Nexagen (prospect -> strategic partner) pushed a commercial term in their most recent redline that would grant them exclusive reseller rights for our Prompt Optimization module in North America for 12 months, plus a benchmark clause that would trigger price protection if their peers secure a lower public list price (effectively a MFN/price parity ask). They are also asking for a 20% introductory discount and a revenue guarantee tied to the benchmark.

Why I'm escalating: legal flags MFN-type clauses as company-level risk (pricing leakage + precedent). Exclusivity + benchmark together expose us to commercial lock-in across GTM and channel. Deal size and signal: first year committed ARR of ~$1.25M with a potential expansion to managed services in year two. Procurement is requesting a signed agreement by 05/07.

Ask: 1) Exec sign-off if we will consider a time-boxed, highly-scoped exclusivity (or any exclusivity at all) and 2) authorization for a counter on the benchmark language (acceptable alternative suggestions below).

Suggested mitigations (initial thoughts):
- Exclusivity: if any, limit to a single named product SKU (Prompt Optimization v1), North America only, and 6 months max with clear performance milestones.
- Benchmark: reject MFN-style language. Offer a narrowly scoped price review tied to documented procurement events, with a cap on total credits (e.g., no more than 10% of committed ARR or $125k).
- Discount: one-time 12% pilot discount (not 20%) tied to signed case studies/press if possible.

Attachments: Nexagen_Redline_v3.docx (customer redline), Revenue_Forecast_Nexagen.xlsx (internal).

I need a quick legal read + an executive decision point (yes/no with conditions) by EOD 05/03 if we want to keep momentum.

Thanks,
Alex Martinez
Account Executive — Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>, Deal Desk <dealdesk@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-02T11:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Nexagen - exclusivity + benchmark (escalation)

Alex / team,

Thanks for the context and the redline. High level legal position: this is high-risk and we should avoid broad MFN/benchmark clauses and open-ended exclusivity. A few points:

1) Exclusivity: we do not grant territory- or channel-wide exclusivity for production-grade modules. If leadership wants to consider exclusivity, it must be: (a) product-module specific, (b) time-limited (max 90-180 days), (c) subject to measurable performance KPIs (revenue or adoption thresholds), and (d) include termination for failure to meet KPIs.

2) Benchmark / MFN: MFN obligations expose us to market price discovery and retroactive crediting that can cascade. We should refuse MFN; counter with a fixed rebate cap (explicit dollar cap or percentage of the committed ARR) and a requirement that any competitor pricing be independently verified and publicly available.

3) Pricing: a 20% introductory discount is steep. If leadership is open to concession, suggest a single-use 12% discount tied to customer success-level deliverables plus an addendum allowing us to terminate discounts on renewal if terms are violated.

4) Operational controls: any acceptance must be conditioned on logging the commitment in Deal Desk, notifying Finance (for revenue recognition implications), and adding an automatic rollback clause for subsequent public price changes.

Attached is a proposed counter redline (I highlighted the exclusivity duration and a rebate cap). If leadership does not want to negotiate exclusivity, recommend inserting a reseller-preference clause instead (right of first negotiation for a specific product line, rather than exclusivity).

I'm marking this as "high-risk commercial" and recommend escalation to Evelyn for commercial approval.

- Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Counsel, Commercial
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-03T08:33:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Nexagen - exclusivity + benchmark (escalation)

Evelyn,

Quick commercial note from Sales: Nexagen is a strategic OEM partner target — they bring channel penetration into several accounts we are prioritizing. If we walk away on exclusivity now, we risk losing the opportunity to position Redwood as their default optimization provider (they are evaluating two other vendors). First-year ARR is ~$1.25M, expected CAC payback ~6 months with managed services expansion expected year 2 (~$600k incremental).

Timing pressure: procurement indicates they need an agreement signed by 05/07 to meet Q2 onboarding. If we agree to a heavily scoped exclusivity and the capped benchmark credit Rishi proposed, we believe we can close this week.

If leadership prefers a hard no on exclusivity, we need to decide immediately so I can prepare fallback pricing and counter language for procurement.

Marissa Cole
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-03T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Nexagen - exclusivity + benchmark (escalation)

Team — after reviewing the deal economics and Rishi's analysis:

Decision (executive approval, conditional):
1) Exclusivity: APPROVED but tightly scoped — Exclusivity limited to Prompt Optimization v1 only, North America, for 6 months from signature, contingent on Nexagen achieving 80% of the committed ARR in the first 120 days. If they miss the KPI, exclusivity terminates automatically. No channel-wide exclusivity.
2) Benchmark / MFN: REJECT MFN. We will offer a price-review mechanism instead with a hard credit cap equal to 10% of year-one committed ARR (max $125,000). Credits are one-time and do not alter list pricing for future customers.
3) Discount: APPROVED one-time 15% introductory discount (to be applied to year-one subscription fees only) conditional on execution of a press/customer case study and completion of legal review of the redline.
4) Operational requirements: Deal Desk must add the final approved redline to the contract repository, Finance must be notified (cc finance@redwood.ai) before signature, and AM/CS must schedule a 30/90/180-day adoption check with Nexagen. Rishi to finalize language with the specified caps and KPI triggers.

This is a strategic partnership; I don't want precedent to become policy. Record this as an exception with the above guardrails.

Evelyn Hart
VP, Revenue Strategy & Partnerships
Redwood Inference
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Oliver Dunn <oliver.dunn@nexagen.com>, Nexagen Legal <contracts@nexagen.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Bcc: Deal Desk <dealdesk@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-03T17:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Nexagen - exclusivity + benchmark (escalation)

Oliver / Nexagen team,

Thanks for the patience. Leadership has approved a limited path forward. The executive decision includes: a 6-month, product-scoped exclusivity for Prompt Optimization v1 in North America (with KPI trigger), rejection of MFN in favor of a one-time credit cap, and a 15% introductory discount tied to a case study commitment.

Rishi will push the final counter-redline (attached) with the exact KPI thresholds and the credit cap language. Can we aim to review the redline and confirm by 05/06 so we can execute before your procurement deadline?

Next steps: Legal (Nexagen and Redwood) to align on final language. Once agreed, Deal Desk will process signature workflows.

Thanks — looking forward to closing.

Alex Martinez
Account Executive — Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference
